text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Jordan marks the anniversary of King Hussein's assumption of his constitutional powers on May 2, 1953.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali heads to Qatar on Saturday; the visit aims at boosting bilateral ties.
- Fakhri Qawar wins Jordanian Writers Association elections; the new head of the union emphasises the necessity of toughening its stance on opposing cultural normalisation with Israel.
- A Jordanian-Omani summit in Muscat on Saturday; King also attends his nephew Prince Ghazi's wedding to daughter of a prominent Omani.

- Interior minister attacks head of the Moslem Brotherhood for suggesting the government would not hold fair elections next November; says the Islamists are prejudging the situation and indicates they are not optimistic about the outcome.
- Zuhair Khoury elected as chairman of Housing Bank while Abdul-Qader Dweik now promoted to general manager after the bank's AGM (Annual General Meeting) on Friday.
- Government inclined to exempt package tours to the kingdom which are prompted by local travel agents of income tax.
- Sandstorm arrives to Aqaba after damages in property in Egypt.
